data.name: richTextBox1.Text
data.value:
Layered Clothing is comprised of zones and levels.
A zone corresponds to a part of the body and the level is the order in which the clothing should be worn. Level 1 is the closest to the skin, and level 10 would be the farthest from the skin. RAGS preloads three body zones for you. They are "Lower Body", "Mid Body", and "Upper Body". You can add to these zones, say, a "Head" zone, or delete all the zones and create your own custom zones.
One piece of clothing may occupy more then one zone and level. This is perfectly fine. Just assign as many zones and levels as required.
Ex: Socks could be "Lower Body Level 1", Shoes could be "Lower Body Level 2", and say a dress could be "Upper Body Level 2 and Mid Body Level 2".
There are two commands that use the layered clothing scheme.
Item: Layered Wear and Item: Layered Remove
These commands enforce layered clothing limits. Since clothing may or may not be worn after the command runs, you will need to check the status of the item and see if its worn, if you need to do additional commands after its successfully worn. All text displays to the player are automatically handled by the command. You no longer need to display text telling the player their item is worn or removed.
Here are the enforced rules by the layered clothes engine using our socks and shoes as an example. Shoes(lvl 2) may be worn without Socks(lvl 1). Socks(lvl 1) can not be worn if Shoes(lvl 2) are currently worn, or if another pair of Socks(lvl 1) are already worn. Socks could not be removed if Shoes(lvl 2) are also already worn. For Items that span multiple zones, the same rules apply, the are enforced at each level.

data.name: label60.Text
data.value: Here is a layered clothing example: Let's look at this model to the right. We could design his clothing objects in the following manner. His socks would be Lower Body 1, the shoes could be lower body 2. His boxer shorts could be mid body 1, and the pants are mid body 2. His under shirt is upper body 1, and his long sleeved shirt is upper body 2. This is a very simple example, and you can add body zones and clothing levels as you see fit.

data.name: label46.Text
data.value: Status Bar Items appear at the bottom of the Rags Player window and usually hold useful variable data for the player. You will want to reference a variable typically when creating your Status Text. Some common examples for status text might be: Name: [playername] or Cash: [v: playercash]. Please visit the online help for a complete list of text references you can use.
